chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Hilal from Ula'a ibn Razin from Muhammad ibn Muslim from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked him about the meat of horses and mules, and he said, 'It is permissible, but people dislike it.' And this report does not contradict what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: Is the meat of horses and mules halal or haram in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the meat of horses and mules is inherently halal, distinguishing the legal ruling from the cultural aversion ('i'af') people have toward consuming it. This establishes a clear precedent in Shia jurisprudence where permissibility is not negated by customary dislike, aligning with the broader principle that all living creatures are permissible unless explicitly prohibited.
